title: Rigveda 6.14: To Agni
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 6.14: To Agni: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 6.14 is a hymn of 6 verses addressed to Agni. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 6, the family book of Bharadvāja. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 415r-415v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 6.14.1-2 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 5, varga 16); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 415r
translation.original_text:
1a̱gnā yo martyo̱ duvo̱ dhiya̍ṁ ju̱joṣa̍ dhī̱tibhi̍ḥ | bhasa̱n nu ṣa pra pū̱rvya iṣa̍ṁ vurī̱tāva̍se ||
2a̱gnir id dhi prace̍tā a̱gnir ve̱dhasta̍ma̱ ṛṣi̍ḥ | a̱gniṁ hotā̍ram īḻate ya̱jñeṣu̱ manu̍ṣo̱ viśa̍ḥ ||
translation.text:
1WHOSO to Agni hath endeared his thought and service by his hymns, That mortal eats before the rest, and finds sufficiency of food.
2Agni, in truth, is passing wise, most skilled in ordering, a Seer. At sacrifices Manus' sons glorify Agni as their Priest.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 415r (numbered 88r by the scribe) (OPenn image 415, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 6.13.4 ‹saḥ deva prati vāram›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 415v (numbered 88v by the scribe), begins in RV 6.14.3 ‹aryaḥ tūrvantaḥ dasyum āyavaḥ›. Verses 6.14.1-2 end on this page.
translation.edition_text:
1agnā | yaḥ | martyaḥ | duvaḥ | dhiyam | jujoṣa | dhīti-bhiḥ | bhasat | nu | saḥ | pra | pūrvyaḥ | iṣam | vurīta | avase
2agniḥ | it | hi | pra-certāḥ | agniḥ | vedhaḥ-tamaḥ | ṛṣiḥ | agnim | hotāram | īḷate | yajñeṣu | manuṣaḥ | viśaḥ

translation.original_ref: RV 6.14.3-6 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 5, varga 16); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 415v
translation.original_text:
3nānā̱ hy a1̱̍gne 'va̍se̱ spardha̍nte̱ rāyo̍ a̱ryaḥ | tūrva̍nto̱ dasyu̍m ā̱yavo̍ vra̱taiḥ sīkṣa̍nto avra̱tam ||
4a̱gnir a̱psām ṛ̍tī̱ṣaha̍ṁ vī̱raṁ da̍dāti̱ satpa̍tim | yasya̱ trasa̍nti̱ śava̍saḥ sa̱ṁcakṣi̱ śatra̍vo bhi̱yā ||
5a̱gnir hi vi̱dmanā̍ ni̱do de̱vo marta̍m uru̱ṣyati̍ | sa̱hāvā̱ yasyāvṛ̍to ra̱yir vāje̱ṣv avṛ̍taḥ ||
6acchā̍ no mitramaho deva de̱vān agne̱ voca̍ḥ suma̱tiṁ roda̍syoḥ | vī̱hi sva̱stiṁ su̍kṣi̱tiṁ di̱vo nṝn dvi̱ṣo aṁhā̍ṁsi duri̱tā ta̍rema̱ tā ta̍rema̱ tavāva̍sā tarema ||
translation.text:
3The foeman's wealth in many a place, Agni, is emulous to help. Men fight the fiend, and seek by rites to overcome the riteless foe.
4Agni bestows the hero chief, winner of waters, firm in fray. Soon as they look upon his might his enemies tremble in alarm.
5For with his wisdom Agni, God, protects the mortal from reproach, Whose conquering wealth is never checked, is never checked in deeds of might.
6O Agni, God with Mitra's might call hither the favour of the Gods from earth and heaven. Bring weal from heaven that men may dwell securely. May we o'ercome the foe's malign oppressions, may we o'ercome them, through thy help o'ercome them.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 415v (numbered 88v by the scribe) (OPenn image 416, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 6.14.3 ‹aryaḥ tūrvantaḥ dasyum āyavaḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 416r (numbered 89r by the scribe), begins in RV 6.15.2 ‹saḥ tvam su-prītaḥ vīta-havye›. Verses 6.14.3-6 end on this page; 6.14.3 begins on fol. 415r (numbered 88r by the scribe).

4agniḥ | apsām | ṛti-saham | vīram | dadāti | sat-patim | yasya | trasanti | śavasaḥ | sam-cakṣi | śatravaḥ | bhiyā
5agniḥ | hi | vidmanā | nidaḥ | devaḥ | martam | uruṣyati | saha-vā | yasya | avṛtaḥ | rayiḥ | vājeṣu | avṛtaḥ
6accha | naḥ | mitra-mahaḥ | deva | devān | agne | vocaḥ | su-matim | rodasyoḥ | vīhi | svastim | su-kṣitim | divaḥ | nṝn | dviṣaḥ | aṃhāṃsi | duḥ-itā | tarema | tā | tarema | tava | avasā | tarema
